chunks: 5. Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah al-Barqi (may Allah have mercy on him) said: My father narrated to us, from his grandfather Ahmad ibn Abu Abd Allah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fudal, from Ali ibn Uqbah, from his father, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abd Allah al-Sadiq, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of Allah smiled one day until his teeth were showing, then he said: 'Will you not ask me why I smiled?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'I am astonished at the Muslim man that there is no decree that Allah, the Mighty and High, decrees for him except that it is good for him in the outcome of his affair.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Allah's decree for a Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid underscores the Shia concept of 'khair' (goodness) in divine decree, emphasizing that every event, whether perceived as pleasant or difficult, serves a beneficial purpose for the believer's ultimate spiritual outcome. It reflects the theological assurance that Allah’s wisdom is perfect and that trust in Him (tawakkul) leads to recognizing the hidden goodness in all circumstances. The narration highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) role in guiding the Ummah to view trials as opportunities for growth and reward.
